subject.title: enhancement: Optimize voice message processing pipeline for Telegram

question: What Telegram voice pipeline contract should OpenClaw support before implementation: narrow early feedback only, async/background TTS delivery, a priority voice lane, or a full staged STT/TTS pipeline with state snapshots?
rationale: The request crosses Telegram ingress ordering, audio preflight, TTS delivery, caching, telemetry, and session-state semantics, so source inspection cannot safely choose the permanent behavior contract.

options.title: Design staged async STT/TTS
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker, land or reject narrow typing and delivery-mode slices separately, then design async delivery with ordering, state snapshots, and live benchmarks.

options.title: Limit near-term scope
options.body: Treat immediate typing cues and separate text/voice delivery as the supported near-term UX fixes while leaving deeper queueing, streaming, and caching unplanned.

options.title: Reject pipeline rewrite
options.body: Close broad background voice pipeline work for now and direct users to tune existing audio/TTS providers, timeouts, and Talk-mode surfaces.

recommendation.title: Design staged async STT/TTS
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker, land or reject narrow typing and delivery-mode slices separately, then design async delivery with ordering, state snapshots, and live benchmarks.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is around inbound concurrency, Telegram context runtime, and queue/debounce behavior, which are the product contracts this issue must settle first.
